input.message:
S6 is on PR #411 (feat/checker-watch, stacked on feat/instantiation-probe, trail #278 linked). The loud-failure and 300-edit memory parts of the gate pass. The 25 ms p95 passes only for a component with few props of its own in a Chakra-sized program (22.6 ms). It fails for a component built on Chakra's ButtonProps (p95 565 ms at best), and no sound design closes that gap.

- **Design.** On the pinned tsrs 0.23 and the Go 7.1 beta, `updateSnapshot` only takes effect with `ensurePrograms: true`. Without it, an edit is missed even when notified. With it, an edit nobody announced is still missed, so it would be served from the old text with no sign. The kept snapshot is therefore updated with exactly the files the session announced; `WatchSession` now sends every change it applies (new `SemanticProvider::changed`). Before each answer, every file the checker's program read (1,855 for Chakra) has its modification time and size compared with what it had when read. This costs about 1.5 ms. An unannounced change makes that answer come from a fresh snapshot, with a warning naming the file. Why this design: content hashing costs too much on this program, and trusting the session's notifications alone cannot detect a miss. Files modified within 2 s of a read are re-read every time instead. 64-program and RSS recycling are unchanged; a replaced process takes its snapshot with it.
- **ButtonProps edit-and-query** (300 edits, shared machine at load 10–29): p50/p95/p99 ranged 433/565/838 to 520/1,161/2,727 ms; the base branch measured 458/605/882 to 546/1,015/1,461. Wall-clock tails tracked machine load more than the change. The load-independent number is the checker's CPU per edit, down from 437–737 ms to 56–80 ms.
- **What bounds it:** caliper converting ButtonProps' 1,140 props, which takes 330–375 ms even on an unchanged snapshot. Getting under 25 ms would need converted types cached across snapshots, which needs the dependency closure the ADR lists as unsolved.
- **Recommended budget:** keep 25 ms for the checker's part only (the new `--props own` mode of the harness; base measured 83 ms there). Give the ButtonProps form the first-answer budget, since its cost is the same conversion.
- **RSS:** peak 321–357 MiB over 300 edits against base 440–455 and the 768 MiB threshold. The 650-edit memory gate peaked at 341 MiB (was 446–478), all 650 answers came from the checker and none were stale.
- **Byte identity:** the edited component plus 10 others, after 300 edits, match a fresh session asked in reverse order — 20,282,789 bytes, the same count as base. Determinism gave nine identical outputs of 341,419,093 bytes, as before. First answer: 435 ms (409–511), no change.
- **Loud-failure test:** `an_edit_the_checker_is_not_told_about_fails_loudly_and_is_answered_from_the_disk` in `crates/semantic/tests/watch.rs`. It runs on tsrs and the Go checker, and fails when the check is disabled. The new tests fail to compile against the base code.
- **Commands (exit 0):** `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just semver`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked --no-fail-fast` (1413 passed), `just test-checker-lane` (now also runs the watch tests), `just test-construct`, and the clean-room run in `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/clean-s6` (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, nextest with the Go checker, watch tests on tsrs).
- **`just gate-measure` exits 1** because first-answer and watch's p95 fail, as expected; memory and determinism pass. I changed the recipe to run all four gates and fail at the end instead of stopping at the first failure.
- **Commits:** 0ae64b68 (feat, with a changeset) and eafb5a25 (docs: ADR 0026 S6 line, `gate-measurements.md`, `type-checker-integration.md`). Signed, no serialized shape or schema change.
- **Not verified:** napi/TS tests (no TS or napi code changed), CI, Linux, and a real Storybook session. Two cases the check does not catch: a file created unannounced where an import failed to resolve, and a tsconfig options change, which still needs a new process.
